title: Sanctioned World API Surface v1
description: The complete set of interfaces a world module may call, and the classes of call it may never make. Enforced by the World Static Analysis Gate as a merge-blocking CI check against every world — official worlds, the reference template, and community submissions alike. This surface is the security boundary for community-contributed code: worlds ship GDScript like any other module, so safety comes from this allowlist plus MANDATORY HUMAN REVIEW, never from an automated-only merge path.
sourceOfTruth: The static-analysis gate loads this file and hardcodes no rule.

derivation.rule: allowedInterfaces is DERIVED from the architecture graph: it is exactly the set of contract names on edges whose SOURCE is a world node. It is never authored from intent.
derivation.why: An allowlist written from memory drifts from the interfaces that really exist, in both directions. Too narrow and the gate rejects legitimate world code; too broad and a world is granted reach the architecture never gave it. A drafted version of this file listed eleven interfaces where the graph gives seven — it had added the controller, input, checkpoint and tuning interfaces, none of which a world has an edge to.
derivation.query: { contracts[e.contractId].name for e in edges if nodes[e.source].label starts with 'World:' }
derivation.enforcement: test/contracts/test_level_contract.gd recomputes this set from the model on every run and fails when this file and the graph disagree. Widening the allowlist by hand is therefore not possible: add the architecture edge and this file follows.

allowedInterfaces.description: The only permitted persistence path. A world never opens, reads, or writes a save file directly, and only under the save keys it declared in its manifest.
Semantic audio event ids. Never a file path, and never a direct AudioStreamPlayer of the world's own.
Declarative hint volumes overriding framing. No custom camera code in a world, in any circumstance.
Register a custom Gill Mod through the Level Contract's optional customAbility element. Travels the same validation a shipped mod does.
Place and configure Drift Fleet units, including the Flagship encounter.
Declare restorable regions and query or advance their state.

deliberatelyExcluded.why: Worlds read player intent through the controller interface and never read raw input (REQ-024 AC-6). There is no world-facing input surface at all, by design.
deliberatelyExcluded.instead: Gate a path on the controller's published movement state, or on a Gill Mod affordance.

deliberatelyExcluded.why: The graph gives no world an edge to the controller. Controller compatibility is DECLARED in world.json, not called.
deliberatelyExcluded.instead: Declare controllerCompatibility in the manifest; the Game Client owns the wiring.

deliberatelyExcluded.why: Checkpoints are declarative. A world places nodes in the checkpoint group and the Game Client wires them to the life and capability systems.
deliberatelyExcluded.instead: Place checkpoint volumes in the scene.

deliberatelyExcluded.why: A world does not read the tuning surface; it declares tuningOverrides in its manifest, limited to the enumerated worldOverridable set.
The HUD reads game state; a world does not write to it. A world that needs to say something to the player says it through a declared element, not by drawing.
deliberatelyExcluded.instead: Use the declarative elements the Level Contract provides.

exclusionPolicy: If a world genuinely needs an excluded interface, the fix is to add the architecture edge and let this file follow — never to widen the allowlist by hand. A world that can only achieve something by reaching outside this surface is evidence the interface is wrong, not evidence the world is special.

enforcement.defaultPosture: deny — a symbol absent from allowedInterfaces is a violation, not an omission

filesystem.rationale: A world module has no legitimate reason to touch the filesystem; persistence goes through the Save Integration Interface.

network.rationale: Single-player, offline game. There is no network layer of any kind.

osExecution.rationale: Executing processes or shelling out from world code is arbitrary code execution on a contributor's machine.

dynamicEvaluation.rationale: Dynamic evaluation defeats static analysis entirely — it is how an allowlist gets bypassed.

rawInput.rationale: Worlds read intent, never input (REQ-024 AC-6). A world gating a path on a physical key could never be rebound, which would break the accessibility guarantee for every player of that world.

multiplayer.rationale: No multiplayer, in any phase — a firm non-goal, not a deferral. This mirrors the Engine Feature Policy applied to core systems, so world modules are covered by exactly the same ban as core (REQ-030 AC-7).

coreInternals.rationale: Reaching past a published interface into a core system's private members is the hole that makes a world unforkable. If a world can only achieve something this way, the interface is wrong — fix the interface, not the world.
symbols: any member prefixed _ on a core system
get_node paths into core/ scene trees
direct instantiation of core system classes not exposed via a sanctioned interface

guidanceOverride: Where general Godot documentation, engine samples, or catalog technology guidance demonstrate RPC-based movement, server-authority patterns, direct file access for saves, or raw Input reads, that guidance DOES NOT APPLY to world modules in this project. Implement world logic as local single-player code against the sanctioned interfaces above.

violationOutput.requirement: Failure output names the offending file, line, the specific forbidden symbol, and the call class it violates, as structured machine-readable output an AI coding agent can parse and self-correct against.
